contractFor02.issuer: App server only, after fresh verifiedUser acceptance of a nonempty subject and reviewed explicit enrollment/login intent; never auto-bootstrap or revive on missing/revoked/unknown scope. Existing verifiedUser length/type check needs nonempty-subject contract qualification before issuance.
sessionRecord: random opaque session id and independent high-entropy capability secret digest
subject from authenticated upstream response, never body/URL/profile
server deployment realm/incarnation, monotonic integer epoch
fixed configured audience origin + /api/state and allowlisted method/scope
server issuedAt/expiresAt, active/revoked status and durable revoke outcome
contractFor02.credentialTransport: Proposed server-set Secure HttpOnly SameSite cookie scoped to reviewed host/path; raw capability never in localStorage, logs or operation body. Public session selector/generation can be compared but has no authority without secret + fresh subject + persisted row. Cookie-based mutation/enrollment/revoke requires reviewed CSRF token or custom-header design plus exact configured Origin; reject duplicate/ambiguous credential sources and cross-origin requests.
contractFor02.trustedAudience: Canonical configured application origin/resource, not arbitrary Host/request body; never broaden /mcp or /api/v1 read tokens into state mutation authority.
contractFor02.admission: For every new mutation, freshly authenticate upstream, then inside the same serialized commit unit read current persisted subject/session/realm/epoch/active/expiry/scope, compare presented binding, validate exact resource/method and input schema, claim operation id, apply state revision CAS, and record terminal outcome. Parameterize SQL. No await to uncoordinated storage after a successful detached admission check.
contractFor02.operationKey: Unique (subject, appSessionId, realm, epoch, operationId), with canonical digest of resource/method/expected state revision/validated mutation payload. Operation id is idempotency only, never authorization. Same key+digest returns prior outcome without a second write only after current authorization; same key+different digest is conflict; another subject/session/generation cannot read or replay it.
contractFor02.revocation: Authenticated same-subject capability, CSRF-protected revoke commits tombstone/increment and outcome in the same ordering domain as mutation. Revoke is idempotent including lost acknowledgments. Never change revoked back to active; explicit later login creates a new random session id/secret. Expired/missing rows do not auto-recreate authority. Epoch counters must not wrap.
contractFor02.logoutOrder: Stop enqueueing writes; request/confirm durable app revoke before reporting app revocation complete, then invoke provider SDK logout separately. Lost/failed revoke response means revocation UNKNOWN/PENDING, never successful cancellation. Retry same revoke id. SDK logout failure cannot restore app grant; app revoke success cannot claim provider logout success.
contractFor02.refreshAndAccountChange: Same verified subject with refreshed/rotated upstream token preserves existing valid app grant; token bytes are not generation. Different subject fails binding. Freeze/discard old-account local responses and require separately enrolled grant for new subject. Cross-tab account transitions cannot reassign a persisted grant.
contractFor02.expiry: Server clock and stored policy only; proposed bounded TTL chosen by Morgan, not body expiresAt. Unknown clock/overflow/storage errors fail closed. Refresh does not silently extend grant lifetime.
contractFor02.responseContract: Committed outcome includes operationId, binding reference, resulting revision, payload digest/version and terminal status. Unknown network/commit acknowledgment remains UNKNOWN, not FAILED/rolled-back. No raw capability or private body in audit/status.
contractFor02.outcomeRecovery: After loss of ack, retry same operation only while authorized. After revocation, mutation retries deny even if prior result exists. A separately authorized same-subject status-only route may return minimal retained terminal outcome after explicit reauthentication; its exact policy must be reviewed. Missing ledger entry after expiry/GC is UNKNOWN, never proof that mutation did not happen.
contractFor02.retention: Keep operation outcomes/tombstones at least the approved maximum retry/offline horizon; beyond it, fail closed to old IDs or require new operation after reconciliation. Do not silently recycle operation IDs or generation keys.

threatAndCorrectness.rule: Ignore as authority; derive subject from verifiedUser and validate persisted app grant. State revision remains concurrency only. Browser storage and user_metadata cannot mint grants.
Preserve app grant if still live; provider rejection still denies. Provider rotation alone cannot revoke or revive app session.

Revoke only selected app session including same-cookie tabs. Other device sessions remain active by explicit recommendation. Different subject never inherits old grant. A stolen still-valid provider token can enroll elsewhere; account compromise needs separate provider/account-wide remedy.

Define linearization at shared storage commit. Revoke first: old-generation mutation cannot commit. Mutation first: persists with ledger outcome, even if reply delayed beyond revoke. Revocation neither compensates data nor proves deletion. Enumerate both orders plus delayed provider check before transaction.

Fresh /user check is a point-in-time provider acceptance. No distributed transaction with provider: provider revoke after that check may race with local commit. App epoch cannot claim to eliminate that window.
Do not infer failure from timeout/abort; retain UNKNOWN and recover status or retry idempotently under authorization. Revoke lost ack retries cannot increment repeatedly or revive old authority.

threatAndCorrectness.case: storage fail / unknown scope / read-replica lag
threatAndCorrectness.rule: Unavailable, stale or missing authority and ledger fail closed. No local-cache acceptance, fallback credential mode or implicit bootstrap. Revocation/admission must share primary linearizable ordering; batch API name alone is insufficient.

A restored old epoch/ledger can resurrect revoked grants and replay writes. Require a durable independent deployment/restore realm not restored with that data; restore procedure rotates realm before serving mutations and invalidates prior app grants. If unavailable, disable mutation admission until requalification. Older handler rollback must not bypass gate.

Bind key and canonical digest to subject/session/realm/epoch/method/resource/revision/payload. Reject altered reuse and cross-resource scope. No exactly-once promise across ledger loss or uncoordinated external side effects.

HttpOnly reduces exfiltration but same-origin malicious script may still submit authorized actions; retain CSP/CSRF/schema validation and avoid claiming XSS prevention from epoch. Never expose/log capability secrets.

s2Prerequisites: Morgan explicitly selects per-app-session invalidation policy, including shared tabs, other devices, app-only logout, re-enrollment and compromise recovery.
Worker02 proposes reviewed server-only issuance/admission/revoke/status interfaces and authorization+CSRF transport; TTL, retry horizon, ledger retention, error/status semantics and bounds are fixed.
Corrected Worker16 review resolves admission/mutation/acknowledgment semantics; full caller requirements remain unqualified.

Qualify actual D1 storage atomic conditional checks, mutation and outcome ledger with revocation serialization, rollback on failed predicates, concurrent writers, primary reads and no legacy bypass; no S2 handler/schema is implemented here.
Approve storage migration/rollback plan, independent restore realm, failure closure and compatible handler rollout before any deployment; no schema deployment authorized by S1.
Run actual composed Worker/D1 and caller SDK/browser race/retry/account-switch tests using selected immutable sources. Synthetic S1 state machine is insufficient as runtime proof.
Any stronger provider-session generation/revocation guarantee requires separate issuer contract and provider evidence; current /user and pinned offline fixture do not establish it.

They assume rather than prove the required production storage primitive; no production epoch/schema/handler exists.
